segments.text: They do, however, reflect the reality of the vaccine injured service members and the concerns of the unvaccinated across the DOD.

segments.text: In January 2021, I came before you as a military whistleblower reporting catastrophic increases in illnesses and injuries across the DOD being reported in the DMIT.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: These concerns were brushed aside by the DOD as data glitches in our defense medical surveillance system.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: It was reported that this computer glitch was fixed.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Per your request for an update,
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Last night, I ran a query in the Defense Medical Epidemiology Database looking at all illnesses and injuries across the DOD.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: As you can see, the total number of reportable events went from 110,000 in 2020 to over 200,000 in 2022.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: The vaccine was introduced into the military in January of 2021.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: A reportable event is defined as an inherent significant threat to public health and military operations.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: A reportable event represents severe life-threatening clinical manifestations that disrupt military training and deployment.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: These numbers are consistent with the over statistically significant rise in vaccine adverse event reports on service members as provided to me by the CDC showing 34,000 reports and 119 deaths.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Compare this senator to the 93 deaths of service members that were attributed to SARS-CoV-2 infection.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
